chunks: Saad narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no harm in a man praying over the deceased after he has been buried."
And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abdillah ibn Muskhan, from Malik, the freedman of al-Jahm, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"If the prayer over the deceased is missed by you until he is buried, then there is no harm in praying over him after he has been buried."
And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu'adh ibn Thabit al-Jawhari, from Amr ibn Jumay', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would pray over the grave if the prayer over the deceased was missed by him."

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray the funeral prayer after the deceased has already been buried?
ai.summary: These narrations from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarify the permissibility of performing Salat al-Mayyit after burial, a ruling supported by the consistent practice of the Prophet and the Imams. This flexibility ensures that the spiritual benefits of the prayer are not lost due to logistical delays, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the continuity of communal duties even after the physical interment.
